sentences.text: Moraxella nonliquefaciens is described as part of the normal human respiratory flora.
Members of its genus are Gram-negative diplobacilli commonly found on skin and mucous membranes.
It has been described as an opportunistic pathogen that rarely causes ocular infection, and reports associate the species with severe endophthalmitis.

Published case reports describe keratitis and endophthalmitis after eye surgery or intravitreal injection, including one patient with common variable immunodeficiency and one on long-term topical corticosteroids.
At genus level, a case-control study reported nasal microbiota dominated by Moraxella species as associated with respiratory health in elderly people.
